messages:
Alex: Hi folks  second day at Redwood. Where should I publish small how-to guides for new services? I want them discoverable but not clutter the main Templates gallery. Any recommended pattern?
Jamie: welcome Alex! :wave: Two places: 1) Canonical templates stay in Knowledge / Templates, 2) team-specific how-tos live in Team Space / Guides. If it's reusable, propose it as a template.
Alex: OK. If I draft a how-to in my Team space and later want to promote it to a shared template, what's the process?
DocsBot: Tip: Promote flow: duplicate -> draft in Team Space -> open a tiny PR in docs-metadata with the page URL and a one-line rationale -> tag the template steward. The PR automations will add it to the Templates backlog.
Alex: Nice. Do we require any front-matter for promoted guides?
Jamie: Yes please add these meta fields at the top: Owner, Audience, TemplateEligibility (yes|no), Tags, and a Short Summary. For runbooks add Severity and Recovery steps.
Alex: Who reviews eligibility? I wrote a quick "service onboarding: api+schema" guide and it includes code snippets and OpenAPI example blocks. Is embedding code OK?
Victor: I review new template asks for infra-related content. Code snippets are fine. Prefer links to small gist or the monorepo path rather than huge pasted blobs. If you include OpenAPI, add a short sample and link to the full spec in repo.
Alex: Got it. How about diagrams (draw.io / Miro) — can we embed or should we link externally?
Jamie: Link externally and add a small PNG preview in Notion. We avoid heavy embeds for performance and permissions reasons. Also add a DiagramVersion tag.
Alex: If the Team space draft uses a template-like structure, how do I keep it in sync when the canonical template changes?
DocsBot: Use TemplateVersion meta and follow the template migration flow. When a canonical template increments major version, owners request teams to migrate within 30 days. We also run a weekly job that reports pages using out-of-date TemplateVersion tags.
Alex: How do I request edit access to a canonical template to fix a minor typo?
Jamie: For small fixes, comment on the template and tag the owner with the suggested edit so they can merge. If it's urgent, submit the Request Docs Access form with page URL and role=editor. Include your employee ID if SSO is blocking.
Alex: Is there a slash command to raise the access request? I prefer Slack workflow.
DocsBot: Yes: /request-docs-access <page-url> <role> — fills the form for you and notifies devex team. It also suggests owners based on page metadata.
Alex: Great. Also curious about search: how do we make sure folks find our team guides?
Victor: Add these properties: Tags (comma list), Component, Audience, and add the page to the Team Space table-of-contents. Also add the keyword list at the bottom under 'Search aliases'. Our search index picks up those aliases.
Alex: One last: deprecation policy? If I promote a guide and later we change APIs, what's the right way to mark it obsolete?
Jamie: Set Lifecycle=deprecated and add a DeprecationDate and ReplacementURL. Owners should set a migration note and notify #eng-notices if it's widely used. DocsBot will surface deprecated pages in weekly run.
IT Support: FYI if anyone sees a 403 when opening Docs metadata links, submit an IT ticket with the Notion URL and your employee ID; we'll check SSO groups.
Alex: Thanks all, I'll draft in Team Space, add meta fields, and open a PR to promote. Appreciate the guidance!
Jamie: Welcome aboard Alex. Ping me if you want a quick review before promoting. :thumbsup:
